summary: Executed backend+frontend auth-rotation verification on preview URL. Core credential rotation/session invalidation flows passed; brute-force threshold and CORS credential posture checks failed.

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout did not trigger after 5 invalid attempts (6th attempt still returns 401; expected 429 per playbook)
CORS responds with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and no Access-Control-Allow-Credentials; cookie-credentialed cross-origin admin auth posture is not explicit-origin based

action_items: Align brute-force policy to lock after 5 failed admin logins if that is the required policy (current code in lib/security.py uses limit=8).
Set explicit CORS origin(s) in backend/.env and ensure allow_credentials=true for cookie-based admin auth when cross-origin support is required.
Update stale regression fixture in /app/backend/tests/test_registration_admin_api.py that still uses old admin credentials (admin@kridangan.local).
critical_code_review_comments: backend/lib/security.py: _login_limiter is configured as limit=8, which conflicts with playbook expectation of 5 failed attempts lockout.
backend/.env + backend/server.py: CORS_ORIGINS is '*' so server intentionally disables credentialed CORS (allow_credentials=False) and returns wildcard ACAO.
backend/tests/test_registration_admin_api.py contains hardcoded old admin credentials, causing future regression drift after credential rotation.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use /app/backend/tests/test_admin_auth_rotation.py as auth regression baseline. Re-run pytest after lockout threshold and CORS origin settings are adjusted. UI login/dashboard/logout flow already validated on preview with username nxtgen.
rca of the issue: 1) Lockout mismatch root cause: security limiter config sets login limit=8 in code, so 6th bad attempt remains 401. 2) CORS posture root cause: backend .env uses CORS_ORIGINS='*', and server.py turns off allow_credentials under wildcard, therefore no Access-Control-Allow-Credentials header is emitted.
